text:
San Jose won this one in overtime on a night when Los Angeles drove the play almost from start to finish. The Kings generated 3.87 expected goals to the Sharks' 1.85 and took 69 shot attempts to 47, which is why the simulated replays give LAK 81 percent of the wins. The gap came from the second period, when SJS scored three times in a span of just under 11 minutes, including Kiefer Sherwood's snap shot on a 1 percent chance and Nolan Allan's wrist shot on a 5 percent look.

Anton Forsberg paid for that. He allowed 3.1 goals more than the 25 shots he faced deserved, and the Sharks led 4-2 after Igor Chernyshov's backhand early in the third. Los Angeles never stopped pressing, out-chancing San Jose 1.43 to 0.52 in expected goals that period. Erik Haula tipped one in at 10:21, and Artemi Panarin tied it with a slap shot at 15:00. Panarin also missed the game's best chance, a 41 percent look in the second that went off target.

Overtime was a short, odd ending to a lopsided game. Chernyshov took a pass from Macklin Celebrini and scored on a slap shot at 3:18, his second goal of the night, for the 5-4 win. Yaroslav Askarov faced 35 shots and finished close to even against expectation, while Chernyshov, the first star, did his damage on just 0.24 expected goals of his own.
